title: Towards Efficient Compiler Auto-tuning: Leveraging Synergistic Search Spaces
problem: Finding the optimal sequence of compiler optimization passes is computationally expensive and difficult to generalize across programs due to the vast search space of possible pass combinations and their complex interactions.
motivation: Auto-tuning is a critical bottleneck for compiler optimization—traditional iterative compilation and ML-based methods suffer from high computational costs, making them impractical for real-world deployment.
method: The approach discovers 'synergistic pass pairs' (chained passes that jointly optimize a specific metric) through K-means clustering on program optimization patterns, then forms these pairs into coresets. A supervised learning model predicts the best coreset for new programs, enabling rapid convergence to near-optimal pass sequences via integrated search strategies.
key_novelty: Leveraging synergistic relationships between compiler passes to reduce search space dimensionality, enabling efficient prediction and ranking of optimal pass sequences via clustered coresets and ML-guided search.
contributions: A coreset-based representation of synergistic compiler pass pairs that captures common optimization patterns across programs
An ML-driven prediction method to identify the most beneficial pass sequence for new programs without exhaustive search
Demonstration of 7.5% average IR instruction reduction vs. -Oz and 13.9% code size reduction across MiBench, CBench, NPB, CHStone in ~5 seconds

metrics.codesize_reduction: 7.5% IR instruction count vs. -Oz; 13.9% codesize with simple search

limitations: Not discussed; limited to CPU target and compiler-level optimization—does not address GPU or specialized accelerator backends.
primary_theme: Efficient compiler pass selection via synergistic pairings and ML-guided search
